MSW 510: This course is designed to introduce social research methods in the context of social work practice.
MSW 560: This advanced research course builds on material covered in the foundation research course about the design, development, and execution of sound scientific practices.
MSW 800: This course is taken at the same time MSW students are placed into their field experience placements.
MSW 800A: This is the first in a three-part series for students to complete Foundations of Field Experience 1 in a part-time format.
MSW 800B: This is the second in a three-part series for students to complete Foundations of Field Experience 1 in a part-time format.
MSW 800C: This is the third in a three-part series for students to complete Foundations of Field Experience 1 in a part-time format.
MSW 801: This course is the student's second social work field education experience in the four-part field education practicum sequence and provides the MSW student with continued direct clinical practice experience in a clinical agency setting.
MSW 801A: This is the first in a three-part series for students to complete Foundations of Field Experience 2 in a part-time format.
MSW 801B: This is the second in a three-part series for students to complete Foundations of Field Experience 2 in a part-time format.
MSW 801C: This is the third in a three-part series for students to complete Foundations of Field Experience 2 in a part-time format.
MSW 802: This is the third course in the four-part field education practicum sequence comprised of a two-part foundation first year sequence and a two-part advanced practice second year sequence.
MSW 802A: This is the first in a three-part series for students to complete Specialized Field Education 1 in a part-time format.
MSW 802B: This is the second in a three-part series for students to complete Specialized Field Education 1 in a part-time format.
MSW 802C: This is the third in a three-part series for students to complete Specialized Field Education 1 in a part-time format.
MSW 811: This course is the first of two in the foundations of clinical social work practice sequence.
MSW 812: This course is the second of two in the foundations of clinical social work practice sequence.
MSW 813: This course explores conceptual frameworks in human development throughout the life span.
MSW 814: This course surveys the history of social welfare policy, services, and the social work profession in the United States.
MSW 815: This course will provide students with foundational concepts, knowledge, values, and skills in clinical social work practice with individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities.
MSW 816: This foundation practice course is the second in a two-course sequence designed to provide M.S.W.
MSW 819: This course will explore the origins and development of selected social variables characterizing the diversity dimensions (including race, ethnicity, class, gender identity, gender expression, geography and nationality) in contemporary U.S. society.
MSW 850: The Diagnosis and Assessment in Clinical Social Work Practice course addresses the etiology, nature, course and treatment of mental health and substance use disorders across the life development cycle.
MSW 855: The Essential Skills for Clinical Social Work Practice course is an advanced graduate course intended for second-year MSW students to reflect, review and consolidate their graduate studies into a coherent and structured plan of practice as social work professionals.
MSW 865: This MSW course provides students with knowledge in clinical social work practice in the area of urban versus rural settings.
MSW 870: This course will examine core theories, dynamics, functions, policies, and ethics associated with the management of private and public child welfare services are analyzed and examined with a particular focus on the knowledge, skills, and competencies necessary to successfully lead organizations providing such services in the environment of today and the future.
MSW 871: This course covers the major problems of at-risk children and youth, including cognitive, communication, behavioral and emotional problems, attachment disorders, trauma, substance abuse, and developmental disabilities noted in the current DSM.
MSW 875: The course examines state and federal laws that govern the funding and operation of child welfare systems; the history of child welfare policies; and, the legal, political, and social forces that influence the structure and function of child welfare systems in the United States.
MSW 876: This course will cover trauma theories and treatments, and conduct an in-depth critical examination of different populations affected by trauma including child abuse survivors, war veterans, and domestic violence survivors, victims of accidents or crimes, and communities and schools that are devastated by abuse, neglect, and addiction.
MSW 880: This course provides students with knowledge of assessment based on the current Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, published by the American Psychiatric Association; psychotropic medications; and social worker roles when interacting with people with mental health issues and interdisciplinary teams.
MSW 881: This course will provide students with foundational concepts, knowledge, values, and skills in clinical social work practice with mental health and substance abuse.
MSW 885: Policy Issues in Mental Health and Substance Use course focuses on contemporary policy issues related to mental health and substance use including social determinants of mental health, treatment and access to care, rights and privacy, systems transformation, and disparities in care are examined in this course.
MSW 886: The course explores the multi-systemic impact of trauma and substance use on the functioning of individuals, families, and communities.
MSW 894: This is the fourth course in the four-part field education practicum sequence comprised of a two-part foundation first year sequence and a two-part specialized practice second year sequence.
MSW 894A: This is first in a three part series for students to complete Specialized Field Education 2 in a part-time format.
MSW 894B: This is second in a three part series for students to complete Specialized Field Education 2 in a part-time format.
MSW 894C: This is third in a three part series for students to complete Specialized Field Education 2 in a part-time format.
